scope.notes: Inventory now totals 573 rows (341 from Exalted: The Lunars/Exalted Players Guide, 220 from a later Savant and Sorcerer / Book of Three Circles pass, plus 12 from a final Exalted Storyteller's Companion pass). Covers Exalted: The Lunars core innate powers (Lunar Shapechanging, the Tell, True Forms, Caste Mark tattooing/Fixing the Caste, Casteless consequences), the full Shapechanging I/II/III Charm trees (with the Deadly Beastman Transformation gift table), the full Body Enhancement I/II Charm trees, the full Unarmed Combat I through V Charm trees plus three further Body Weapon Technique-rooted utility Charms -- completing the entire Unarmed Combat Charm category -- the complete Melee Combat I/II Charm trees (26 Charms), the complete Ranged Combat I/II Charm trees (17 Charms), pp. 149-161/PDF 152-164, the complete Defensive I/II/III Charm trees (21 Charms), pp. 161-167/PDF 164-170, the complete Survival and Healing I/II/III/IV Charm trees (22 Charms), pp. 168-174/PDF 171-177, the complete Perception I/II/III/IV Charm trees (25 Charms), pp. 174-181/PDF 177-184, the complete Stealth Charm tree (6 Charms), pp. 182-183/PDF 185-186, the complete Interaction and Knowledge I/II/III/IV Charm trees (26 Charms), pp. 183-191/PDF 186-194, and the complete Spirit and Sorcery-access Charms (9 Charms), pp. 191-193/PDF 194-196 -- completing every Charm category in Chapter Five. Chapter Four: Traits (pp. 94-115/PDF 97-118) is fully inventoried (24 rows): the five altered Backgrounds (Artifact, Backing, Followers, Manse, Mentor), the three new Backgrounds (Cult, Heart's Blood, Renown) plus their supporting Regions sidebar, all three player Castes (Full Moon, Changing Moon, No Moon) and the Casteless state, the universal Caste anima-effect grants, the Great Curse (this splat's Limit-Trait analog) and its four Virtue-linked thralls (Curse of the Whipped Dog/Heartless Weasel/Drunken Monkey/Raging Bull), the Lunar Anima Banners visibility table, and the Face/Renown social-rank system (Face Trait ranks Urrach-ya through Shahan-ya, the four-category Renown Trait, and the tlak gaining/losing/respecting-face procedures), plus a short Lunars and Regeneration sidebar. No dedicated Lunar-specific Merits/Flaws subsection exists in Exalted: The Lunars itself -- confirmed absent, not merely unreviewed. This edition of Exalted: The Lunars has three player Castes (No Moon, Full Moon, Changing Moon) plus Casteless, not the five-Caste structure (adding Waxing/Waning Moon) introduced in later editions. The universal Merits & Flaws gap is now filled from the Exalted Players Guide: Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (pp. 18-41/PDF 21-44), is fully transcribed (88 rows: 44 merits + 44 flaws), covering every Physical/Mental/Social/Supernatural/Property Merit and Flaw applicable across all five Exalted types, with splat-specific eligibility/cost caveats (e.g. Lunars-only Chimera Flaw; Celestial-Exalted-only Known Anathema, Permanent Caste Mark, Greater Curse, and Throwback Flaws; Abyssals-and-Ghosts-only Death-Taint Flaw) captured verbatim in each row's notes. A later pass then triaged the cross-splat sorcery/artifice supplements Savant and Sorcerer and Book of Three Circles, adding 220 more rows: the complete Chapter Five Terrestrial and Celestial Circle spell catalog (84 selectable spells, cross-referenced to Lunar's own Terrestrial Circle Sorcery/Celestial Circle Sorcery Charms), a 102-entry Hearthstone catalog (15 Sample Hearthstones from Savant and Sorcerer's Chapter Three plus 87 more from Book of Three Circles' Chapter Six 'long roll', all cross-referenced to the Manse (altered for Lunars) Background), a 13-row Artifice and Enchantment catalog from Savant and Sorcerer Chapter Two (the Artifact-rating framework, Drawback/alternate-power-source rules, the five-step creation process, a freshly-read Lunar-specific 'In-Game Creation: The Lunar Exalted' notes row, two named Merits including the moonsilver-relevant Moonsilver Initiate, the Magical Materials catalog, exotic-ingredients examples, and 5 named Sample Artifacts), a 13-row Warstriders appendix (the overview/operation/benefits-limitations/maintenance framework, all five warstrider design classes -- including Royal, explicitly attested to First Age Lunar pilots -- as selectable Artifact-rated equipment, the weaponry-mounting/mundane-weapons/artifact-weapons reference catalogs, and the moonsilver-native Proteus Gauntlet artifact), and an 8-row skim of Chapter One (Magical Theory: the Limits of Sorcery, the Black and White Treatises, the Five Unavoidable Challenges initiation framework, and a freshly-read Lunar-specific 'No Moons' initiation-monopoly sidebar) and Chapter Four (Practical Summonings: the demon/elemental summoning overview, social/political/licensing context, mass summoning rules, and the Bound Spirit Limit Profile system). Per this project's Solar-Circle-Sorcery-eligibility rule, no Solar Circle (Circle of Adamant) content was inventoried for Lunars. This pass adapted the bulk of its content from this project's already-verified Exalted: The Sidereals transcription of the same two source books (identical universal sourcebook prose, re-cited to the same pages), re-verifying only the small number of rows containing genuinely splat-specific commentary, and reading two wholly new Lunar-specific sections (the 'In-Game Creation: The Lunar Exalted' and 'No Moons' sidebars) directly from the source PDF since neither existing inventory had transcribed them. Cross-splat supplements beyond Savant and Sorcerer/Book of Three Circles/the Players Guide are not yet inventoried. A final pass then rendered and read the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's Chapter Two (The Celestial Exalted) Lunar section and Chapter Four (Further Wonders) universal artifact catalog, adding 12 rows: six Lunar-specific Charms embedded in otherwise-narrative Chapter Two prose (Tentacles, Summon Wild Beasts, Acid Spit, Mighty Thews, Strides of the Panther, printed pp. 33-34/PDF 34-35, plus the Counting Coup social debt-and-scar custom, printed p. 28/PDF 29) and six universal cross-splat Sample Artifacts from Chapter Four transcribed here as the master copy for later derivation into the other four families (Ghost Cestus, Sling Bow of Ice, The Golden Viper, Land Ship, Singing Staff, and the Storyteller-adjudicated Eye of Autochthon, printed pp. 77-80/PDF 78-81). That pass brought the inventory to 573 rows. A final pass then added 9 more rows (573 -> 582) freshly transcribed from a sixth source book, Savage Seas, whose Chapter Four "Artifacts of the Waves" section (printed pp. 123-127/PDF 124-128) is a universal, non-splat-restricted naval-artifact catalog -- Cargo Preservation Spindles, Armor of Aquatic Puissance, Steelsilk Sails, Storm Sapphire, Cord of Winds, Wavecleaver Daiklaive, Light Implosion Bow, Lightning Ballista, and a reference-only Artifact Ship Weapons summary table -- adapted from this project's already-verified Abyssal and Sidereal transcriptions of the identical sourcebook prose (same citations, mechanics, and cost; only each row's compatibility text was updated for Lunar), with the Storm Sapphire Effect Table and the Light Implosion Bow/Lightning Ballista dot ratings specifically re-rendered and re-read directly from the source PDF to confirm accuracy. The book's earlier "Magics of the Sea" Charms section (printed pp. 114-122/PDF 115-123) is explicitly Solar/Dragon-Blooded-only per its own text and remains out of scope for Lunar, consistent with the other four families' scoping of this book. No Autochthonia-style setting-restriction caveat applies to any of these 9 rows for Lunar, since Lunars are native Creation-dwellers; several of Lunar's own existing Survival Charms (Whale-Breath Technique, Gill-Breathing Technique, Sealskin Endurance) and the No Moon caste's favored Totem Animals ("creatures of the deep ocean", per this splat's own Castes material) already establish a genuine thematic tie to the sea, so this catalog is recorded with the least-caveated compatibility text of any family's copy.

sources.role: Primary Lunar rules, Charms, Backgrounds, Merits/Flaws, and setting material
Universal Merits & Flaws chapter (Chapter One), applicable across all Exalted types including Lunars

Cross-splat sorcery/artifice supplement; authoritative current Terrestrial (Emerald) and Celestial (Sapphire) Circle spell catalog (Chapter Five) for Lunar's own Terrestrial Circle Sorcery/Celestial Circle Sorcery Charms, plus Manse/Hearthstone (Chapter Three), artifact/enchantment (Chapter Two, including this book's own 'In-Game Creation: The Lunar Exalted' subsection), and Warstrider (Appendix) material. Explicitly supersedes Book of Three Circles except where noted (its own intro states the Hearthstone catalog is the one exception not reprinted here). Solar Circle (Circle of Adamant) content is out of scope for Lunars and was not inventoried.

sources.bookLabel: Exalted: The Book of Three Circles
sources.role: Superseded cross-splat sorcery supplement (image-based PDF, rendered page-by-page); its Terrestrial/Celestial spells and mechanical content are fully superseded by Savant and Sorcerer, but its Chapter Six 'long roll of Hearthstones' catalog is explicitly NOT reprinted in Savant and Sorcerer (per that book's own intro sidebar) and remains the more comprehensive Hearthstone source, reused here from this project's already-verified Exalted: The Sidereals transcription. Its Solar Circle sorcery chapter (Ch4) is out of scope for Lunars.

Cross-splat sourcebook (image-based PDF, rendered page-by-page); Chapter Two's embedded Lunar Charms are Lunar-specific, while Chapter Four ('Further Wonders') is a universal artifact catalog transcribed here as the master copy for later derivation into the other four families.

Cross-splat naval/nautical sourcebook (image-based PDF, rendered page-by-page); Chapter Four's 'Artifacts of the Waves' section (printed pp. 123-127/PDF 124-128) is a universal, non-splat-restricted catalog of naval artifacts, adapted here from this project's already-verified Abyssal/Sidereal transcriptions and spot-checked against freshly rendered pages. Its earlier 'Magics of the Sea' Charms section (printed pp. 114-122/PDF 115-123) is explicitly Solar/Dragon-Blooded-only per the book's own text and remains out of scope for Lunar.

rulesNotes: Printed page numbers in this book run 3 less than the PDF page number supplied (PDF page = printed page + 3) for the copy used to build this inventory; both are recorded on every citation.
Lunar Charms use Minimum Attribute (not Minimum Ability) fields, per p. 122 (PDF 125).

A handful of rows in the Unarmed Combat III-V trees have book text that reads awkwardly around botch/infection resolution (Rabid Beast Bite, Grasping Pseudopod Method); paraphrased faithfully but flagged in each row's notes for a closer re-read before promotion. Armor-Rending Claw Fist's mechanics also cut off mid-sentence at the bottom of its rendered page and needs the following page reviewed to complete it.

Melee Combat I/II and Ranged Combat I/II are now complete (pp. 149-161/PDF 152-164). Several Charm descriptions span a page break in the source (stat block/tree diagram on one page, prose continuing on the next); these were transcribed as single continuous Charms with a note on the page split where applicable. Arrow-Shaping Method cross-references Shaping the Once-Living Form (an existing Shapechanging II Charm row) as a co-prerequisite alongside Nature's Harmony Advantage.

Defensive I/II/III are now complete (pp. 161-167/PDF 164-170). The Defensive-III tree diagram (PDF p. 169/printed p. 166) labels one node 'Limb-Shedding Growth', but the Charm's own header and running text (PDF p. 170/printed p. 167) both read 'Limb-Shielding Growth' -- the Charm's own text was trusted per the standing rule to prefer stated Charm text over tree-diagram lettering when they conflict. Pack-Saving Method references a reduced-cost case tied to a Charm named 'Brotherhood of Lake and River' not yet located elsewhere in this book; no crossReferences entry was added for it pending that Charm's discovery.

Survival and Healing I/II/III/IV are now complete (pp. 168-174/PDF 171-177). Unerring Den-Finding Sense's own Prerequisite Charms line lists only Beast Instinct Method even though the Survival and Healing II tree diagram draws it alongside Food-Scenting Method and Water-Providing Technique feeding into Wolf Endurance Method; the Charm's own text was trusted. Bruise-Relief Technique's cost/rate sentence reads redundantly in the source and is flagged in its notes for a closer look before promotion.

Perception I/II/III/IV are now complete (pp. 174-181/PDF 177-184). Heightened (Sense) Method is one three-part Charm (sight; hearing/touch; smell/taste) that the Perception II/III/IV tree diagrams draw as three differently-labeled root nodes; those labels were recorded as aliases on a single inventory row rather than as separate Charms. Ritual of Lunar Stability's stat block Duration (lunar months) and mechanics text (weeks) disagree on units for the same permanent-Essence-scaled figure; transcribed faithfully as printed and flagged in its notes.

Stealth (6 Charms, pp. 182-183/PDF 185-186) and Interaction and Knowledge I/II/III/IV (26 Charms, pp. 183-191/PDF 186-194) are now complete. Locating Pack-Forming Presence and Brotherhood of Lake and River in the Interaction and Knowledge III/IV trees closed out both previously-open co-prerequisite items on Sense-Borrowing Method and Pack-Saving Method; their crossReferences were updated and their notes removed. Several rows in this range flag illustration cut-offs or garbled/redundant source phrasing (Chameleon Skin Disguise, Lion Roar Method, Pack-Calling Cry) that were paraphrased as faithfully as legible but merit a second look before promotion.
Spirit Charms (4 Charms) and Sorcery-access Charms (5 Charms), pp. 191-193/PDF 194-196, are now complete, finishing every Charm category in Chapter Five.

Chapter Four: Traits (pp. 94-115/PDF 97-118) is now fully inventoried (24 new rows). Expanded Backgrounds: Artifact, Backing, Followers, and Manse are altered only in flavor text (disposition calculated, no new dot table); Mentor is altered with a re-flavored 0-5 dot table measuring closeness to the character's Silver Pact elder-mentor rather than the mentor's personal power. New Backgrounds: Cult (p. 98-99/PDF 101-102, dot table only runs 0-4 in the legible render -- no 5-dot line was found and this is flagged for a second look before promotion), Heart's Blood (p. 99-100/PDF 102-103, separate 0-5 dot tables for animal forms and for Heart's Blood (Human)), and Renown (p. 100/PDF 103, grants bonus starting points in the separate Renown Trait; Casteless may not take it) plus the supporting Regions sidebar (p. 101/PDF 104) that guides which animals a Heart's Blood purchase may represent by homeland.

Chapter Four's Castes confirm this edition of Exalted: The Lunars has only three player Castes -- Full Moon (pp. 102-103/PDF 105-106), Changing Moon (pp. 104-105/PDF 107-108), and No Moon (pp. 106-107/PDF 109-110) -- plus the uninitiated Casteless state (p. 108/PDF 111), not the five-Caste structure (adding Waxing/Waning Moon) from later editions; the 'Caste' framing text on p. 109/PDF 112 explicitly says essence is fixed into 'one of the three castes.' The universal Caste anima-effect grants (any Lunar may spend 1 mote for one of five minor Tell/Caste-Mark/anima tricks) are inventoried separately from the Lunar Anima Banners table (p. 110/PDF 113), which lists Tell/anima visibility bands by Peripheral Essence spent in a scene.

The Great Curse (p. 109/PDF 112) is this splat's Limit-Trait analog, triggered by acting against a Lunar's primary Virtue or failing a Willpower roll against full moonlight; its four Virtue-linked inner-beast thralls (Curse of the Whipped Dog/Compassion, Heartless Weasel/Conviction, Drunken Monkey/Temperance, Raging Bull/Valor, pp. 109-110/PDF 112-113) were each inventoried as their own row.

The Face/Renown social-rank system (pp. 111-115/PDF 114-118) was inventoried as three rows: the Face Trait itself (six named ranks, Urrach-ya through Shahan-ya, plus the Face Requirements table of minimum Renown and other prerequisites per rank), the four-category Renown Trait (Succor/Compassion, Mettle/Conviction, Cunning/Temperance, Glory/Valor -- distinct from the Renown Background, which merely grants bonus starting points toward it), and the tlak ceremony/losing-face/respecting-face social procedures. A short Lunars and Regeneration sidebar (p. 115/PDF 118) closes out the chapter, cross-referenced to the existing Deadly Beastman Transformation and Halting the Scarlet Flow Charm rows.

No dedicated Lunar-specific Merits/Flaws subsection was found anywhere in Chapter Four; the chapter moves directly from New Backgrounds into Castes/Great Curse/Face without one. This is confirmed absent, not merely unreviewed -- the chapter's opening statement says Merits/Flaws otherwise work identically to core Exalted. Likewise, no dedicated Tribe write-up or Tribe-as-Background section exists; Lunar tribes are addressed only through the altered Backing/Followers text and general chapter flavor, not as a discrete character-creation mechanic.

Chapter Four: Traits is now fully inventoried, completing every planned item in the Lunar intake scope drawn from the primary sourcebook. Remaining outstanding work is limited to the untriaged cross-splat supplements (Blood and Salt, Book of Bone and Ebony, Savage Seas, etc.) listed in the top-level intent; see docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/README.md.

The Exalted Players Guide's Chapter One, "Merits and Flaws" (printed pp. 18-41, PDF pp. 21-44), is now fully transcribed (88 pg- rows: 44 merits + 44 flaws), filling the Merits/Flaws gap noted above for Exalted: The Lunars itself. This chapter is universal across all five planned Exalted families; splat-specific eligibility and cost differences are captured verbatim in each row's notes rather than silently applied. Lunar-relevant highlights: the Chimera Flaw is Lunars-only (revoked totem, hybrid Deadly Beastman appearance, bars the Renown Background for true Wyld-touched chimera); Known Anathema, Permanent Caste Mark (silver tattoo for Lunars), Greater Curse (reduces max Limit pool), and Throwback are all Celestial-Exalted-only (Solar/Lunar/Sidereal) and apply to Lunars; Death-Taint is Abyssals-and-Ghosts-only and does NOT apply to Lunars; Dark Fate normally excludes only Sidereals, not Lunars. The chapter ends at printed p. 41/PDF 44 (full-page illustration on p. 42/PDF 43, closing fiction on p. 43/PDF 44), immediately followed by Chapter Two, "The God-Blooded," title page on printed p. 44/PDF 45.

A later pass (following this project's already-completed Abyssal and Sidereal Savant and Sorcerer / Book of Three Circles passes) added 220 rows of cross-splat sorcery/artifice content to Lunar, using Lunar's existing terrestrial-circle-sorcery/celestial-circle-sorcery Charm rows as the enabling prerequisites. It first added the complete Chapter Five Terrestrial and Celestial Circle spell catalog (84 selectable spells, printed pp. 101-138/PDF 102-139, spell-terrestrial-*/spell-celestial-* ids), adapted from this project's already-verified Exalted: The Sidereals transcription of the identical sourcebook prose (mechanics/cost/citation unchanged; only each row's compatibility text was updated from 'Any Sidereal Exalted' to 'Any Lunar Exalted (No Moon caste)'). Per this project's Solar Circle Sorcery eligibility rule, the Circle of Adamant (Solar Circle) spells beginning with Abjuration of the Maidens were not inventoried for Lunars. It then added the full 102-row Hearthstone catalog (15 Sample Hearthstones from Savant and Sorcerer Chapter Three, printed pp. 66-71/PDF 67-72, plus 87 more from Book of Three Circles Chapter Six's 'long roll,' hearthstone-botc-* ids), similarly adapted from the Sidereal inventory and cross-referenced to Lunar's own manse-background-altered row.

The same pass then added a 13-row Artifice and Enchantment catalog from Savant and Sorcerer Chapter Two (printed pp. 23-41/PDF 24-42): the Artifact rating framework, the Drawback-subtype/alternate-power-source rules, the five-step artifact creation process, and two named Merits (Starting Workshop; Moonsilver Initiate, whose 2-point-for-Lunars cost the book itself calls out) and the Magical Materials catalog and Exotic Ingredients examples, all adapted from Sidereal with compatibility text updated for Lunar's own moonsilver-centric artifact culture -- plus a wholly new 'In-Game Creation: The Lunar Exalted' row (artifact-creation-lunar-notes) read directly from the source PDF (printed pp. 35-36/PDF 36-37), since neither the Abyssal nor Sidereal inventory had transcribed this splat-specific subsection. Five named Sample Artifacts (Collar of Dawn's Cleansing Light, Mask, Ring of Being, Wings of the Raptor, Soul Mirror) round out the 13 rows. It then added a 13-row Warstriders appendix (printed pp. 144-160/PDF 145-161): the overview/operation/benefits-limitations/maintenance framework rows, the five basic design classes as selectable Artifact-rated equipment (Scout, Common, Noble, Royal, Juggernaut -- Royal is explicitly attested to a 'scant handful' of First Age Lunar pilots per the book's own text, one of the few warstrider classes with documented Lunar use), the weaponry-mounting/mundane-weapons/artifact-weapons reference catalogs, and the moonsilver-forged Proteus Gauntlet (which already grants Lunars its full Magical-Material bonus without the double-Essence surcharge non-Lunars pay). Finally, an 8-row skim of Chapter One (Magical Theory, printed pp. 10-15/PDF 11-16) and Chapter Four (Practical Summonings, printed pp. 71-99/PDF 72-100) added the Limits of Sorcery, the Black and White Treatises, the Five Unavoidable Challenges initiation framework, and the four Chapter Four summoning/limit-profile rows adapted from Sidereal, plus a wholly new 'Lunar Sorcery Initiation: the No Moon Monopoly' row (sorcery-lunar-initiation-notes) transcribing Chapter One's 'No Moons' sidebar (printed p. 15/PDF 16) directly from the source PDF -- this sidebar sits immediately beside the 'Sidereals' sidebar the Sidereal inventory already transcribes, but neither prior inventory covered it since it was out of scope for their own splats. This pass brings the inventory to 561 rows; source-manifest.json's sources list was updated to add savant-and-sorcerer and book-of-three-circles, following the same citation convention Sidereal's manifest already established for these two books.
